identity.confidence: XVAL. The 4.0 is the well-trodden one; both surveyed codebases and the earlier community work (my-whoop, whoomp, openwhoop) target it. Its model string is stored as either '4.0' (wizard-paired) or the legacy bare 'WHOOP' row, which resolves to gen5 instead; the skin-temp family resolver bug in the NOOP lineage came from exactly that mismatch, so this manifest claims only the explicit 4.0 spellings and lets the bare 'WHOOP' fall through to whoop5.

standard_gatt.confidence: XVAL. On the 4.0 the standard heart-rate profile answers before any bond, which is why a just-works link is enough to read a live pulse; the custom service opens with a single just-works write rather than the authenticated pairing the 5.0 demands.

commands.name: toggle_realtime_hr
commands.note: 0x03. Starts the live HR/RR stream on the custom channel; realtime data comes back as packet type 0x28 (40). Does not need the feature-flag handshake below.

commands.name: get_hello
commands.note: 0x23 = GET_HELLO_HARVARD, sniffed directly from a 4.0. [CONFLICT] The surveyed repos used 145 for both generations; the gen5 hello is 145, but a wire capture shows the 4.0 hello as 0x23. Settle against our own 4.0.

commands.name: set_clock
commands.note: 0x0a. Clock sync, sent early in the app's init sequence.

commands.name: toggle_standard_hr
commands.note: 0x0e. Makes the strap broadcast on the standard GATT heart-rate characteristic (0x2A37).

commands.name: get_battery_level
commands.note: 0x1a. Response is u16 deci-percent on gen4, unlike the gen5 direct percent.

commands.name: feature_flag_query
commands.note: 0x75. Begins the feature-flag exchange (the app runs 0x75, then 0x76 many times, then 0x78 many times).

commands.name: feature_flag_next
commands.note: 0x76. Iterates the feature-flag exchange; the app sends it about thirteen times.

commands.name: set_feature_flag
commands.note: 0x78. Sets one feature flag per write; the app sends it about eleven times. See enable_sequence.

commands.name: get_data_range
commands.note: 0x22. Response carries the last-synced page sequence as LE32 at bytes 10..13.

commands.name: send_historical
commands.note: 0x16. Requests the historical buffer replay (packet type 0x2f).

commands.name: historical_ack
commands.note: 0x17. Advances the read pointer; deletes nothing. HISTORY_COMPLETE arrives as metadata (type 49) command 3.

commands.name: force_trim
commands.note: 0x19 = FORCE_TRIM. Irreversibly deletes the buffer up to the write head. Never send until HISTORY_COMPLETE has arrived and at least one record came back; a mis-sequenced trim cost the fourth source five hours of data.

enable_sequence.confidence: Flag names and opcode are [SERIES], sniffed from a 4.0 (the app sends about eleven set-flag writes; six names are captured here). The payload dimensions (32-byte name field, 40-byte payload) are INFERRED from the gen5 format the third source pinned, since the two generations share the command enum; they are unconfirmed on gen4. Each value byte is taken as 1 (enable). This handshake unlocks deep-data packets and is not needed for live heart rate, which toggle_realtime_hr starts on its own.

time.confidence: XVAL for the fields, [WRS] for the payload-relative byte positions: layout offsets are into the inner record (payload[0] = packet type), where the timestamp sits at 2 and HR at 8 on BOTH generations — the survey numbers (gen4 6/10/12, gen5 plus 4) counted from the full frame, whose header is 4 bytes on gen4 and 8 on gen5.

confidence_note: Realtime, command subset, and the historical record decoders. Packet 47 records route by inner byte [1] (the version): gen4_v24 (also v12) decodes the DSP block (HR body[14], R-R body[15]/[16], gravity three f32 from body[33], SpO2 red/IR raw ADC body[61]/[63], skin-temp register body[65:67], respiration body[73:75]); gen4_v5 (also v7/v9) decodes the generic HR+R-R record; gen4_v25 decodes the PPG-buffer record's gravity triplet (i16/16384 from body[66]). v24 and v25 are backed by real 4.0 capture goldens imported from tanarchytan/whoop-rs [WRS] (fixtures/records/gen4_v24_v1.json, gen4_v25_v1.json); v5 has no real capture yet and is pinned by an invariant round-trip test. The skin-temp RAW register is now admitted, but its absolute °C scale stays a deferred per-device learned anchor: the gen4 scale is in [CONFLICT] between sources with no calibration golden, so no temperature is claimed here (ADR-009). Unknown version bytes decode to a typed DECODE_UNKNOWN_RECORD_VERSION rather than the guess-fallback the upstream RE uses; Maverick admits only mapped versions. Nothing is hardware-verified by this project yet.
